paper_metadata.title: Provable bounds for noise-free expectation values computed from noisy samples

experiments.description: QAOA for MAXCUT on a random 3-regular graph with 40 nodes/qubits, evaluated on IBM Sherbrooke at depths p=1 and p=2 using classically optimized angles and CVaR-based postprocessing.

algorithm.variant: QAOA for MAXCUT with CVaR evaluation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classically optimized angles from light-cone simulation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per binary variable; 40-node 3-regular graph mapped to 40 qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: MAXCUT on a random 3-regular graph; equivalent to maximizing the cut value.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal cost Hamiltonian for MAXCUT (not explicitly written in the paper text).

problem_instance.description: Random 3-regular graph MAXCUT instance from Ref. [11].

dataset_specification.description: Random 3-regular graph with 40 nodes; optimal cut value reported as 56.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical light-cone simplification used to evaluate 2-local expectation values by simulating at most 14 qubits at a time.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: p=1 run with 10^5 shots; p=2 run with 10^7 shots; compare noisy expectation, noise-free expectation from classical simulation, CVaR, best sampled value, and global optimum.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; Pauli-Lindblad model discussed theoretically; experiments run without twirling
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: staggered dynamical decoupling; CVaR postprocessing; layer fidelity analysis
noise_model.mitigation_details: No twirling in the main experiments; staggered dynamic decoupling applied; CVaR evaluated at alpha chosen from layer fidelity.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Sherbrooke ECR/CNOT-equivalent hardware-native two-qubit gates
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Light-cone optimized classical simulation for parameter optimization.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Sort sampled objective values and compute CVaR; compare against classical optimum and noise-free expectation values.

speedup_claims.conditions: for extracting good bit strings from noisy quantum computers under the Pauli-Lindblad/layer-fidelity model
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a lower-bound style guarantee for sampling probabilities, not an unbiased expectation-value estimator.

speedup_claims.factor: CVaR variance scales as O(1/alpha), and with alpha=1/sqrt(gamma) this gives O(sqrt(gamma))
speedup_claims.baseline_method: probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) variance scaling O(gamma^2)
speedup_claims.conditions: for Bernoulli/Normal-like cases discussed in the paper
speedup_claims.caveats: PEC provides unbiased estimators; CVaR provides bounds, not unbiased estimates.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QAOA depth p with sampling overhead proportional to sqrt(gamma)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: For 3-regular graphs, p<=3 can be classically optimized by simulating at most 30 qubits at a time (as cited).

experiments.description: QAOA for a hardware-compatible higher-order Ising spin-glass problem on 127 qubits, evaluated on IBM Sherbrooke for depths p=1 to p=5 with parameter transfer and CVaR analysis.

algorithm.variant: QAOA for higher-order Ising spin glass with parameter transfer
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Heuristically obtained QAOA angles via parameter transfer from same-structure problems; verified with MPS simulation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per vertex on a heavy-hex-compatible graph; linear, quadratic, and cubic Ising terms implemented via parity computation on qubits in V2.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize a random coefficient higher-order Ising Hamiltonian with linear, quadratic, and cubic Z terms.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_v d_v Z_v + sum_(i,j) d_{i,j} Z_i Z_j + sum_l d_{l,n1(l),n2(l)} Z_l Z_{n1(l)} Z_{n2(l)}

problem_instance.description: Random heavy-hex-compatible higher-order Ising spin-glass instance on the full 127-qubit IBM Sherbrooke lattice.

dataset_specification.description: Random coefficients chosen from {+1, -1} with equal probability on a heavy-hex graph; optimal solutions computed using CPLEX.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Parameter transfer used to obtain angles; MPS simulation with bond dimension 2048 used to verify expectation values.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each p evaluated with 10^5 shots; compare noisy expectation values, noise-free expectation values from MPS, best sampled value, and fitted CVaR alpha.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; experiments run without twirling
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: staggered dynamical decoupling; CVaR postprocessing; layer fidelity analysis
noise_model.mitigation_details: No twirling in the main experiments; staggered dynamic decoupling applied; CVaR evaluated at alpha fitted from noise-free expectation values.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Sherbrooke heavy-hex hardware-native two-qubit gates
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Parameter transfer and MPS verification; parity computation/uncomputation for ZZ and ZZZ terms.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bootstrap estimation of CVaR variance; compare noisy expectation values, fitted CVaR, and best sampled values.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: direct sampling from the noisy circuit
speedup_claims.conditions: for the layer-fidelity-based bound on extracting good samples
speedup_claims.caveats: The required overhead becomes impractically large for the 127-qubit instance because layer fidelities are low.

speedup_claims.factor: CNOT depth 6p independent of system size n
speedup_claims.baseline_method: generic implementation of higher-order Ising terms
speedup_claims.conditions: for the heavy-hex-compatible graph construction used in the paper
speedup_claims.caveats: This is circuit-depth scaling, not an algorithmic runtime speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: CNOT depth 6p independent of system size n; sampling overhead proportional to sqrt(gamma).
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Optimal solutions computed with CPLEX; MPS verification with bond dimension 2048.

experiments.description: Twirled versus untwirled QAOA on the same 127-qubit higher-order Ising problem, comparing output distributions and fitted CVaR values on IBM Sherbrooke.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with and without Pauli twirling
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Same fixed QAOA angles as the untwirled/twirled comparison in Appendix A; not separately specified.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 127-qubit higher-order Ising model as the main 127-qubit experiment.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the same higher-order Ising Hamiltonian.

problem_instance.description: Same 127-qubit heavy-hex higher-order Ising instance, evaluated with and without twirling.

dataset_specification.description: Same random coefficient instance as exp_2.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Twirling inserts additional single-qubit gates, increasing pulse schedule duration by about 8%.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100,000 shots total for each of p=1 and p=2, with 1,000 random twirls and 100 shots per twirl in the twirled case; compare CDFs and fitted alpha values.

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise with and without Pauli twirling
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: Pauli twirling; staggered dynamical decoupling; CVaR postprocessing
noise_model.mitigation_details: 1000 random twirls, 100 shots each; compare twirled and untwirled distributions and fitted alpha values.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bootstrap used to estimate standard deviations of fitted alpha values.

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment is a twirling comparison study; no speedup claim is made.
